questions.question: What is the syntax to declare an array in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, arrays are declared using the syntax 'type[] variableName' or 'type variableName[]'.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'length' property in Java arrays?

options.text: To get the maximum value in the array
To get the minimum value in the array
To get the number of elements in the array

questions.explanation: The 'length' property in Java arrays returns the number of elements in the array.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid way to initialize a string in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, strings can be initialized using the 'new' keyword or using string literals.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'charAt' method in Java strings?

options.text: To get the length of the string
To get the character at a specific index
To convert the string to uppercase
To convert the string to lowercase

questions.explanation: The 'charAt' method in Java strings returns the character at a specific index.

questions.question: How do you access an element in a Java array?

options.text: Using the array name followed by the index in square brackets
Using the array name followed by the index in parentheses

questions.explanation: In Java, you can access an element in an array by using the array name followed by the index in square brackets.

questions.question: How do you declare a multidimensional array in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, multidimensional arrays can be declared using the syntax 'type[] variableName[]' or 'type variableName[][]'.

questions.question: How do you initialize an array in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, arrays can be initialized using the 'new' keyword.

questions.question: What is the result of using the '+=' operator on a String object in Java?

options.text: It appends the new string and creates a new object
It appends the new string and modifies the existing object
It overwrites the existing string with the new string

questions.correctAnswer: It appends the new string and creates a new object
questions.explanation: In Java, using the '+=' operator on a String object creates a new String object and assigns it to the original variable, it does not modify the original String object.

questions.question: How do you sort an array of integers in ascending order in Java?

options.text: Using the 'sort()' method from the Arrays class
Using a for loop and swapping elements manually
Using a while loop and recursion

questions.correctAnswer: Using the 'sort()' method from the Arrays class
questions.explanation: In Java, you can use the 'sort()' method from the Arrays class to sort an array of integers in ascending order.
